channel.title: Grand Lakes Community and Water Districts Portal
channel.description: Resource site for the Grand Lakes community and water districts (MUDs and WCID).

item.title: Know the Consultants Serving the Grand Lakes Water Districts
item.description: Foundational Series: Know Your Water District. The private firms (attorney, operator, bookkeeper, auditor, financial advisor, engineer, tax collector, delinquent-tax attorney, trash contractor, and web hosting provider) serving the Grand Lakes Water Districts. Said firms are generously compensated to serve, advise, and defend the interests of said districts. They do the opposite...

item.title: Grand Lakes Community Maps
item.description: Foundational Series: Know Your Water District. Grand Lakes community maps showing the voter precincts and jurisdiction of the four water districts serving the neighborhood.

item.title: Know Your Water District Board
item.description: Foundational Series: Know Your Water District. Recognizing that the legal system was being leveraged as an expensive wall against them, Grand Lakes residents took their grievances directly to the ballot box. In the local election on May 2, 2026, the Grand Lakes community turned out and voted out long-standing board members, marking a major turning point toward accountability and signaling a clear warning to remaining district consultants...

item.title: Structure of the Grand Lakes Water Districts
item.description: Foundational Series: Know Your Water District. This introductory article presents the structure of the Grand Lakes Water Districts. How the water district business is exploited by private firms (attorney, operator, bookkeeper, auditor, financial advisor, engineer, tax collector, delinquent tax attorney, trash collector, and web hosting provider) generously compensated to serve, advise, and defend the interests of said districts.

item.title: Guide: The Texas Public Information Act in Brief
item.description: Foundational Series: Know Your Water District. This introductory article talks about the Texas Public Information Act (PIA). What is public information, why district records matter to the public, the public's right to know, public information requests, withholding information, and more.

item.title: Guide: The Texas Open Meetings Act in Brief
item.description: Foundational Series: Know Your Water District. This introductory article talks about the Texas Open Meetings Act (OMA), the district's obligations when it comes to conducting official business, and the public's role in ensuring that the power they entrusted government with is exercised lawfully.

item.title: Who Controls a Water District?
item.description: Foundational Series: Know Your Water District. This introductory article talks about the controlling authority within a water district. The board is the governing authority. Consultants are advisors; they are not the government, they do not run the government, they do not have any governmental authority.

item.title: The Legal, Ethical, Moral, and Civic Duties of Water-District Consultants
item.description: Foundational Series: Know Your Water District. This introductory article talks about the legal, ethical, moral, and civic duties of water-district consultants. They advise, perform, document, and report within their respective areas of responsibility, but are not the governing authority and must never take advantage of the board.

item.title: The Legal, Ethical, Moral, and Civic Duties of Water-District Boards
item.description: Foundational Series: Know Your Water District. This introductory article talks about the legal, ethical, moral, and civic duties of water-district boards⎯obeying the law, exercising independent judgment, stewardship, identifying conflicts, transparency, supervising consultants, and more.

item.title: What Is a Texas Water Control and Improvement District (WCID)?
item.description: Foundational Series: Know Your Water District. This introductory article talks about Water Control and Improvement Districts (WCIDs); their functions, powers, governance, and why their business and affairs matter to the residents. The distinction between MUDs and WCIDs is also discussed.

item.title: What Is a Texas Municipal Utility District (MUD)?
item.description: Foundational Series: Know Your Water District. This introductory article talks about Municipal Utility Districts (MUDs); their functions, powers, governance, and why their business and affairs matter to the residents and taxpayers.

item.title: 📜 An Open Letter to the Twenty Board Members of the Grand Lakes Water Districts
item.description: An open, community-centered letter tailored for the board members across the Grand Lakes water districts. It appeals to their civic duty, directly addressing how the withholding of direct contact information—orchestrated by legal counsel—undermines true public service and creates a shield for third-party exploitation.

item.title: ✉️ Template Letter to District Board Directors
item.description: A template letter designed to help residents ask clear, targeted questions about where their tax dollars are going. It emphasizes fiduciary duty and requests specific details on transparency, consultant contracts, professional fees, annual expenditures, and RFQs to secure competitive contracts.

item.title: The Principles of Lawful Governance
item.description: A meaningful governance framework for Municipal Utility Districts and Water Control and Improvement Districts must be built on commitments to Independence, Transparency, Compliance, Oversight, Justice, and Accountability. This guide presents acronyms to help our community explore the aforementioned foundations, principles, and values. The acronyms constitute a proposed governance and accountability framework; they are not a substitute for applicable Texas law or the district's statutory duties.

item.title: Understanding the System: TCEQ & The Texas Water Code
item.description: Understanding the System (TCEQ & The Texas Water Code)... To help our neighborhood dive deeper into their research, here is a breakdown of the structural loopholes that allow the issues we face to occur, along with the specific state agencies involved.

item.title: Know Your Rights Guide: How to Request Public Records Under the Texas Public Information Act (PIA)
item.description: Know Your Rights Guide: How to request public records under the Texas Public Information Act (PIA).

item.title: Attending the Water District Monthly Meetings
item.description: Strategy guide for attending the Grand Lakes water district monthly meetings, asking questions, and checking the minutes.

item.title: 📅 🗓️ Grand Lakes Water District Meeting Calendar and Watch
item.description: The Grand Lakes water district boards make crucial decisions on invoices, budgets, tax rates, operations, infrastructure projects, contracts, agreements, water/wastewater rates, and more. Such decisions impact the lives and finances of each and every resident served by the district. How can we, the residents and taxpayers, ensure that said decisions are done properly, fairly, and lawfully, following impeccable due diligence?

item.title: Taking Back the Board: How to Run for a Grand Lakes MUD/WCID Seat
item.description: How residents / taxpayers must run for office if we need to take back control of the Grand Lakes water districts. If not, we are giving compromised consultants the opportunity to defraud us for another 40 years.

Share what you discovered during this challenge with your neighbors, friends, teacher, class, and us!

item.title:

Water district leaders make big decisions about our water, taxes, infrastructure, finances, transparency, compliance, and more. By asking big questions surrounding such topics, we protect our neighborhood. Not paying attention comes with a high cost!
